body.statement: If \(P\) is homogeneous of degree \(r\geq1\) and \(\det G_P\equiv0\) in \(\mathbb R[S3]\), then symmetry of the second derivative gives \(\mathrm dG_{P,X}\{Q_P(X)\}=0\). Consequently \(Q_P\{\mathcal T_P(X,t)\}=Q_P(X)\) and \(P\{\mathcal T_P(X,t)\}=P(X)\) for every \(X\in S3\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).
body.justification: This is the direct \(d=3\) specialization of the dimension-free adjugate-translation identity and retains the note's original notation.
body.gap: The dimension-free proof derives the adjugate direction from Hessian symmetry under the half-weighted trace-pairing convention; that derivation is not supplied by the general quasi-translation literature.
body.consumer: The three-dimensional classification may continue to cite this notation-compatible specialization, while the general rigidity theorem cites the dimension-free lemma.
body.proof_tex:
Apply the all-dimensional adjugate-translation lemma with \(d=3\), \(S_d=S3\), and the polynomial \(P\) appearing here.  Its trace-pairing gradient and adjugate are exactly \(G_P\) and \(Q_P\) from the frozen definitions.  The hypothesis \(\det G_P\equiv0\) is the determinant hypothesis of that lemma; homogeneity is not needed for this step.  The lemma therefore gives
\[
 \mathrm dG_{P,X}\bigl(Q_P(X)\bigr)=0,
 \qquad
 Q_P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=Q_P(X),
 \qquad
 P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=P(X)
\]
for every \(X\in S3\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal T_P\), these are precisely the asserted identities.
